pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered from 00:48:55 — onboarding call with Trevor, custom plan around schedule, body and goals, everything loaded into an app, film-and-correct video loop on every new movement, weekly check-in forms with weight progress and adjustments. Asked for questions he had none and instead re-stated why he needed it: 'No. Doing it solo hasn't worked for me. It just hasn't.' Agreement without curiosity — he asked nothing about how the programming would handle his hypermobility, his displaced vertebra or his knees, and neither did the rep.

Delivered in a single compressed sentence inside the recap: 'The nutrition protocol is going be great for you because it's designed around longevity and how do we actually create eating habits and routines and how do we implement two, three, four principles that makes it easy and sustainable... so we're not stressing about meal prepping.' Accepted without comment. Thin treatment given that he had named diet as his own biggest weakness — 'that's probably one of the biggest chinks in my game, like in the armor' — and had identified planning effort as the specific failure mode the pillar claims to solve.

Delivered as the cell phone number, weekly check-ins and a community of guys doing the same programme. This was the pillar he bought into and he volunteered why, at length and tied directly to his own history: 'it's support, really... I don't want to feel like I'm doing this by myself,' and 'I want somebody who's actually good at the [stuff]... Just being able to be like, yo, I have a question. And he's right there with it. I don't have to wait two weeks.' When asked what stood out most across the whole presentation he named this. His entire past-failure story is friends and trainer friends going silent for a week or two, so responsiveness is the product feature that matters most to him.

anchors.raw: this is a relatively unique skill. Like you could search up you can search up any videos you want on YouTube it's not like I absolutely you know can't can't figure out something for myself
anchors.competitor: YouTube and free online kettlebell content
anchors.note: He had already been researching kettlebell training on video before the call and knows the information is free. He also has a gifted mobility programme from an Australian couple that he rates well but does not use. He resolves the anchor himself — what he is buying is presence, not information — which is the strongest possible setup for the accountability pillar and was not converted into value against price.

anchors.raw: it's not that I couldn't ask my homies. My trainer friends and stuff would be like, yo, can you show me some kettlebell stuff? She's like, I don't really know stuff that has to do with kettlebell.
anchors.competitor: Trainer friends in his social circle
anchors.note: He has qualified trainers in his network who would help for free, and he pre-emptively dismissed them on two grounds — they do not know kettlebells, and they leave him waiting a week or two for a reply. A rare anchor the prospect demolishes himself; the rep did not pick it up.

anchors.raw: So for me, it'll be closer to like 8, right?... All right. So 6,000 USD CAD. Yeah. 8424. Okay. Well, that's the part that I was concerned about, right?
anchors.note: The second non-US prospect in this batch for whom the conversion materially changed the reaction to the number. He also immediately re-expressed the price as a monthly rate — 'so that's a K a month, right?' — which framed it against a monthly surplus of roughly $500 CAD, making the offer visibly impossible in one step.

anchors.raw: my roommate's awesome, too. Like, he's in crazy good shape. He's like, approaching 60, and this man can, those 75 pound logs, he's like picking them up... The dude can deadlift 300 pounds.
anchors.note: He lives with and works alongside conspicuously fit people — a roommate approaching 60 who outworks him, fitness-trainer friends he describes as badasses, and ceremony elders he does not want to resemble. Desire is fully formed and needs no building, which is why he rated the programme 8 out of 10 before hearing the price. The only missing variable was money.

unmet_demand.want: Conditioning for Sundance — four to six hours of dancing daily for four days without food or water, starting nine days after this call
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer is a six-month progressive programme that begins with an onboarding call and video-corrected movement acquisition. It is not a nine-day event-preparation product and cannot be. The rep nonetheless positioned it as one — 'that's almost a reason to actually jump on board the kettlebells ASAP' — which sells a benefit the programme is not structured to deliver in that window.

unmet_demand.want: Programming that safely accounts for generalised joint hypermobility with unstable knees and a vertebra displaced by a fall onto concrete
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Both were disclosed clearly and neither was addressed by anyone on the call. Loaded ballistic kettlebell work in a hypermobile trainee with a spinal injury is exactly the case that needs clinical input, and the offer contains no clinical component and no clearance step. Whether the programme can serve him safely is genuinely unknown.

unmet_demand.want: An entry point he can actually fund — roughly $500 CAD a month spare, two maxed credit cards, no savings and about $100 in his account
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is $6,000 USD and the rep judged a payment plan at $500 a month unworkable, additionally indicating some financing route was unavailable to him as a Canadian. The improvised fallback of a $1,000 USD self-serve product is still roughly $1,403 CAD, about three times his entire monthly surplus, so it does not solve the problem either.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that he and Trevor would actually work well together before committing to six months of one-to-one coaching
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked directly and got no answer at all. There is no trial call, no introductory conversation and no sample of Trevor offered anywhere in the process, so a prospect buying six months of a relationship with a coach he has never spoken to has no way to test it. This is very likely solvable and simply is not addressed.
